=={{header|Cxc}}==

Cxc has no <code>while</code> loop; iteration folds into the atom lifecycle. The <code>main</code> atom carries no fields: the counter <code>n</code> flows through the <code>tick</code> message payload as a trampoline. Each arm pattern-matches the payload, prints <code>word_for(n)</code>, and enqueues the next tick with <code>n + 1</code> until the terminal guard <code>n > 100</code> fires the arm whose target is <code>end</code>.

The <code>word_for(n: Int!)</code> observation reads as a direct transcription of the problem statement. Four guarded arms cover the cases in source order: multiples of 15 yield <code>"FizzBuzz"</code>, then multiples of 3 yield <code>"Fizz"</code>, then multiples of 5 yield <code>"Buzz"</code>, and the fallback <code>|?: n.to_string()</code> covers the remainder. First-arm-wins dispatch does the heavy lifting; the <code>n % 15</code> arm must precede the <code>n % 3</code> and <code>n % 5</code> arms for correctness.

<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
def main:
    word_for(n: Int!) :- String!
        ||: n % 15 == 0 : "FizzBuzz"
        ||: n %  3 == 0 : "Fizz"
        ||: n %  5 == 0 : "Buzz"
        |?: n.to_string()

    -> running
        self :> tick(1)

    running <: tick(n: Int!):
        |: n > 100 -> end
        |: else    -> running
            print(self.word_for(n))
            self :> tick(n + 1)
</syntaxhighlight>

Parameterised observations take named args and bind them as locals in the body. <code>n</code> flows into every guard and the fallback body through lexical scope. Outer observations declared on an atom and inner bindings inside an observation body share one shape: <code>name :- expression</code>; the body itself is just an expression, and <code>||: … |?: …</code> is that expression here.

Inside an observation, <code>||: guard : body</code> is an expression-position multi-arm dispatch: the first arm whose guard holds yields its body value, and the closing <code>|?: body</code> covers the no-match case. The two glyphs together replace <code>if</code> / <code>else if</code> / <code>else</code>; cxc has no <code>if</code> expression at v1.0.

The receive-side uses a grouped shape: <code>running &lt;: tick(n: Int!):</code> opens the group and binds <code>n</code> from the payload, and each arm hangs beneath as <code>|: guard -&gt; target</code>. First-match dispatch in source order fires the terminal arm when <code>n &gt; 100</code> holds, and the <code>|: else</code> fall-through arm runs the self-loop body otherwise. <code>:&gt;</code> is an asynchronous self-send that enqueues the next <code>tick(n + 1)</code> on the atom's own serial dispatch queue; args are snapshotted at enqueue.
